newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus to issue new banknotes.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus to issue new banknotes.

text.p: New 10, five and one pound notes will go into circulation on Tuesday in Cyprus for the first time in more than 15 years, the governor of the Central Bank of Cyprus said on Monday.

"The issue of a new series of banknotes was considered necessary for the effective upgrading of the security features on the Cypriot bills," central bank governor Afxentis Afxentiou told a news conference.
It was generally accepted, he said, that banknotes should not remain in circulation for more than 15 years.
Existing notes, in circulation since 1977 and 1979, will continue to be legal tender while banks start collecting the bills to gradually replace them with new ones, he said.

The new notes show changes in design, drawn from the history, folk art and flora and fauna of the island. The new notes are one millimetre smaller in size than existing bills. But 10 pound notes will still be green, fivers purple and one pound notes brown.

"Additional security elements have been included in the new notes which are adapted to modern technology and the requirements of control and processing procedures in automatic machines. They are in all respects on a par with notes of the European Union and other advanced countries," Afxentiou said.
The new notes carry a map of Cyprus in intaglio printing of optically variable ink which changes colour from gold-light brown to green-light grey depending on the angle of viewing.
The watermark of the Cyprus moufflon goat has been replaced with a bust of Greek goddess Aphrodite and a grey security thread runs through it, bearing the letters KTK.

The one, five and 10 pound notes are being printed by French company Francois Charles Oberthur. The printing of the new 20 pound notes is being carried out by Thomas De La Rue of Britain. They are due to enter circulation by the end of 1997.

Central bank officials said 30 million bills have been ordered of notes with a nominal value of 20, 10, five and one pound. They are aimed aimed at covering the needs of the market for the next two to three years.
